facts.title: One coordinated housing pathway
facts.text: House Delivery brings together precision manufacturing, coordinated purchasing and Canadian construction. Engineered housing systems, procurement, manufacturing and construction partners are coordinated around the project. Scope, site work, assembly, permitting and completion responsibilities are agreed before commitments are made.

facts.title: Construction systems
facts.text: Light-gauge steel, domestic timber or other suitable engineered construction methods may be considered for a project. Many collection designs identify precision light steel frame. The appropriate system and site-specific Canadian engineering must be confirmed; a catalogue rendering does not establish an approved construction specification.

facts.title: Housing projects across Canada
facts.text: House Delivery welcomes housing conversations with developers, municipalities, First Nations and Indigenous communities, non-profits, institutions and individuals across Canada. Discuss location, housing mix, land, infrastructure and local delivery arrangements. National positioning does not guarantee service availability, production allocation or delivery dates for a particular project.

facts.title: Multi-home development
facts.text: A project can start with a discussion about one home or a multi-home housing program. For 20, 50, 100 or 500+ homes, first establish the community or developer objectives, province, housing mix, land and servicing status, phasing, approvals, funding readiness and local delivery capacity. Numbers discussed are planning scenarios, not confirmed capacity or a delivery commitment.

facts.title: First Nations and community-led housing
facts.text: Start with the Nation’s housing needs and priorities. Home selection and project planning can consider cultural expression, privacy, gathering, multigenerational living, local design priorities and local participation or assembly training. Requirements and participation arrangements are developed with the community; there is no automatic funding eligibility or employment guarantee.

facts.title: Municipal and institutional projects
facts.text: For municipalities, non-profits and institutions, begin with the intended households, target housing mix, available site, servicing, planning pathway, procurement requirements and project objectives. A personal project review is needed to establish feasibility and responsibilities.

facts.title: Home-package pricing
facts.text: The current advertised Premium home-package rate is CAD $250 per sq. ft.; Signature is CAD $300 per sq. ft. These are home-package planning rates, not completed-construction prices or a firm project quotation. The applicable design, measured area, scope and current project-specific pricing need confirmation.

facts.title: Budget and scope exclusions
facts.text: Allow separately for project-specific site work, foundations, local assembly and construction, freight and delivery, taxes, permits, engineering, services, local completion and other project-specific costs as applicable. Confirm the written project scope before budgeting or committing. A package estimate must not be presented as a turnkey or occupancy cost.

facts.title: Premium, Signature and the inclusions library
facts.text: Premium offers controlled refinement in materials, finishes and detailing. Signature offers selected higher-touch materials and feature finishes. The inclusions library also represents Essential preliminary selections; this does not establish a current advertised Essential home-package rate. Confirm each home’s available tiers and final inclusions in its Design Studio and project review.

facts.title: Design Studio and customization
facts.text: Explore the model’s available Premium and Signature selections in its Design Studio, review room looks and coordinated finishes, and create a Look Book. Changes to layouts, exterior expression or specifications require review for engineering, compliance, availability, price and scope. An image or saved selection is a design intention, not approval for construction or a binding supply commitment.

facts.title: Your Look Book
facts.text: The model page’s Design Studio and Look Book help organize available selections and communicate design intentions for project review. Selections and PDFs do not replace final scope, technical review or approvals. The Concierge cannot retrieve private saved projects, Look Books, customer records or account data; use the existing project tools or ask the team for help.

facts.title: CMHC Pre-Reviewed catalogue terms
facts.text: CMHC catalogue designs are Pre-Reviewed reference designs, not blanket permits or pre-approval for a property. Local adaptation, site-specific Canadian engineering, code review, foundations and the relevant authority’s approvals remain necessary. The dedicated CMHC Terms & Conditions page provides the official terms PDF, attribution and explanations. The catalogue reference date is February 14, 2025.

facts.title: Property and feasibility review
facts.text: Check zoning and permitted use, lot dimensions, access, setbacks, height, servicing, drainage, site conditions and local requirements before selecting a design for a property. The existing Check My Property pathway is a preliminary review, not a permit or guarantee of eligibility. It is focused on supported BC/Lower Mainland jurisdictions; other locations require a personal project review.

facts.title: Timing and delivery planning
facts.text: The project pathway includes feasibility and scope, design and selections, local engineering and approvals, coordinated manufacturing and procurement, delivery and Canadian construction. The schedule depends on the site, approvals, confirmed scope, freight and construction arrangements. Request a project-specific review; no guaranteed manufacturing, permit or occupancy date is published here.

facts.title: Working with your builder
facts.text: House Delivery welcomes conversations with an existing builder to review the housing system, site work, assembly and finishing responsibilities. Canadian construction arrangements and the division of responsibilities are established for the project.

facts.title: A personal project review
facts.text: The House Delivery team can review your location, organization, housing type, approximate number of homes, land or site status, timing and key objectives. Contact details and your reviewed project summary are sent only when you explicitly request follow-up. An inquiry does not subscribe you to marketing.
